column1: # Lane  Package that must not share its runner with other packages. Each reviewed lane is pinned to
# -p=1: one package at a time, so its tests own all four vCPUs. Two kinds of package live here:
#   - media certification: synthetic playout targets with strict latency or capacity assertions;
#   - CPU-heavy packages whose own parallel tests need a runner to themselves (#1570).
# Separate runners overlap the lanes without allowing package concurrency inside any of them. The
# highest lane number is the lane count (scripts/go-shard.sh); .github/workflows/ci-go.yml's matrix
# names each lane as certification-<lane>/<count>.
# internal/integration is here for balance. Its tests are serial, so it gains little from a runner
# of its own.
# internal/playout/watermark renders and compares frames on every core. In an ordinary -p=4 lane it
# measured 445s to 619s beside three other packages, over the per-package cap (#2716).
# internal/api serves the channel packager's HLS and MPEG-TS (#1512 phase 2c).
# internal/demolibrary encodes filler and scans the tree in parallel tests. Sharing an ordinary
# -p=4 lane it measured 743s; at -p=1 it measures 138s to 235s (#2716).
# internal/platform/store is CPU-heavy, not latency-sensitive: its SQLite tests run in parallel
# (#1631) and every statement runs through the race detector's view of a pure-Go SQLite. Beside api
# and playout its lane passed the 15-minute timeout; alone it measures about 460s (#2716).
# internal/channels/schedule runs under -race and again without it (go-race-policy.sh), and its
# seasonal walks are hundreds of CPU-seconds of parallel subtests. Sharing an ordinary -p=4 lane the
# two runs measured 836s and 730s; at -p=1 they measure about 200s and 150s (#2716).
